results.summary_before: This project implements a simple 32-bit RISC-V processor core with 8 general-purpose registers. It includes a boot select input, UART receive and transmit pins, and eight bidirectional GPIO pins. The design is intended to be tested over the demo board USB UART, but no test has been implemented yet. External hardware includes a boot mode selector, a UART interface, and GPIO connections.

results.summary_before: This project contains a two-stage operational amplifier designed by Majid Sami ALakl for the TT08 shuttle. It has three analog pins: two inputs (INN and INP) and one output (OUT_Maj). Testing can be done using a Digilent Analog Discovery 3 for various measurements. The design is a straightforward analog building block with minimal documentation.

results.summary_before: This project implements a single-ended operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using a folded cascode architecture. It operates from a 1.8V supply and has differential inputs (INp and INm) and a single output (OUT). Testing involves applying a differential input signal and observing the output with an oscilloscope. The design is a basic analog building block with limited documentation.

results.summary_before: This project attempts to create a random number generator by exploiting the unstable state of a latch when both set and reset are low. It includes 34 instances per output pin to increase the chance of randomness. The design can be frozen to sample values, and inputs allow selecting different instances. The documentation is humorous and uncertain about whether it will work, acknowledging potential bias.

results.summary_before: This project implements a Dynamic Power Management Unit for a System on Chip in SystemVerilog. It dynamically adjusts voltage and frequency levels based on inputs such as performance requirements, temperature, battery level, and workload, using a finite state machine to manage transitions between power states. The documentation is very brief and does not describe the pin functions or testing procedure in detail. No external hardware or specific test setup is mentioned.

results.summary_before: This Verilog design models a PLC-based electric vehicle motor controller with PWM speed control, power and mode selection, headlight, horn and indicator outputs, and overheat warning. Inputs come from separate PLC and HMI control lines, and the design drives motor speed bits, a PWM output and status LEDs. The documentation lists recommended external hardware but the section is truncated, so the exact bill of materials is not fully specified. It is notable for packaging an automotive-style control system into a single Tiny Tapeout tile, though no silicon test results are given.
